evidence.title: Diagnostic criteria for diabetes and prediabetes
evidence.source: American Diabetes Association, Standards of Care in Diabetes
evidence.text: Diabetes may be diagnosed by fasting plasma glucose of at least 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L), 2-hour plasma glucose of at least 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) during an oral glucose tolerance test, HbA1c of at least 6.5% (48 mmol/mol), or a random plasma glucose of at least 200 mg/dL in a patient with classic symptoms of hyperglycaemia. Without unequivocal hyperglycaemia, diagnosis requires two abnormal test results. Prediabetes is defined by fasting glucose 100-125 mg/dL, 2-hour glucose 140-199 mg/dL, or HbA1c 5.7-6.4%.

evidence.title: Sepsis-3 definitions and the qSOFA score
evidence.source: Singer et al., JAMA 2016;315(8):801-810
evidence.text: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. In adults with suspected infection, quick SOFA (qSOFA) criteria of respiratory rate of 22/min or greater, altered mentation, and systolic blood pressure of 100 mmHg or less identify patients more likely to have poor outcomes when two or more criteria are met. qSOFA is a prompt for further assessment, not a stand-alone diagnostic test for sepsis.

evidence.title: National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS2)
evidence.source: Royal College of Physicians, 2017
evidence.text: NEWS2 aggregates scores for respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, supplemental oxygen, systolic blood pressure, pulse rate, level of consciousness or new confusion, and temperature. An aggregate score of 5 or 6, or a score of 3 in any single parameter, should prompt urgent review by a clinician competent in assessing acutely ill patients. A score of 7 or more is the threshold for an emergency response, including assessment by a team with critical-care competencies.

evidence.title: Heart attack warning signs
evidence.source: American Heart Association
evidence.text: Warning signs may include chest discomfort, discomfort in other upper-body areas, shortness of breath, cold sweat, nausea, or lightheadedness. The American Heart Association advises calling emergency services when heart attack warning signs occur. Local emergency numbers and protocols vary.

evidence.title: Stroke warning signs (F.A.S.T.)
evidence.source: American Stroke Association
evidence.text: Stroke warning signs include face drooping, arm weakness and speech difficulty. Time to call emergency services is critical when any of these appear, and local emergency numbers vary.

evidence.title: CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine equation for eGFR
evidence.source: Inker et al., N Engl J Med 2021;385:1737-1749
evidence.text: The 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation estimates glomerular filtration rate without a race coefficient, using serum creatinine, age, and sex. Chronic kidney disease is classified by GFR category (G1 90 or more, G2 60-89, G3a 45-59, G3b 30-44, G4 15-29, G5 below 15 mL/min/1.73m2) together with albuminuria, and requires abnormalities persisting for more than three months.

evidence.title: Metformin use in patients with reduced kidney function
evidence.source: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Safety Communication, 2016
evidence.text: FDA revised metformin labelling to base kidney-function decisions on eGFR rather than serum creatinine. Metformin is contraindicated in patients with an eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m2. Starting metformin is not recommended when eGFR is between 30 and 45, and for patients already taking it whose eGFR falls below 45 the benefits and risks of continuing should be assessed. Kidney function should be assessed before starting and at least annually.
